findings.issue: The production build and server (npm build / npm start) run on nitro 3.0.260903-beta, a pre-release package; nitro v3 is still in beta/RC (latest dist-tag 3.0.261029-rc, 2026-10-30), so the server runtime can see breaking changes.
findings.suggestion: This is the officially mandated path for TanStack Start 1.0, so keep it — but rely on package-lock.json (already present), keep the caret-prerelease pin, and schedule an upgrade once nitro v3 ships stable, re-running the production build test.

findings.issue: The whole app rests on TanStack Start 1.169.4, whose 1.0 stable release is 18 days old (2026-10-13); expect rapid minor-releases and possible behavior churn.
findings.suggestion: Watch TanStack Start release notes and bump deliberately; keep the current clean separation (all server functions in app/src/lib/server.ts) so framework changes stay cheap.

findings.issue: resolve.tsconfigPaths and Vite 8's Rolldown pipeline are young (Vite 8 stable 2026-03-12), a second recently-introduced layer the team inherits.
findings.suggestion: Nothing to change — Vite 8 is required by Start 1.0 and the option is documented stable; just treat Vite major upgrades as part of the Start upgrade cycle.

summary: This app is forward-leaning but clean: zero experimental flags or unstable_ names, and it consistently uses the current stable spellings (validator, shellComponent, nitro/vite) rather than RC-era or experimental APIs like RSC. The real novelty is infrastructural: TanStack Start 1.0 (stable 2026-10-13) plus Vite 8 plus a mandated nitro v3 beta running the production server. The beta is exactly where the framework's docs say to put it, contained to two config files, and lockfile-pinned, so risk is real but well-managed.
